(p-489) Sūrat al-An'ām

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿All praise is due to Allah﴾ This teaches the wording and the meaning together, with an allusion to His independence: that is, the praise belongs to Him even if you do not praise Him. ﴿Who created the heavens and the earth﴾ He used the plural for "heavens" because they are layered, one above another. As for the earth, although it is seven according to the majority (of scholars), its layers are not one above another; rather, some of them are adjacent to others. The verb ja'ala (to make/create/place) takes one object when it means "to originate and bring into being," as in His saying: ﴿and made the darknesses and the light﴾; and it takes two objects when it means "to transform/make," as in His saying: ﴿And they make the angels, who are servants of the Most Gracious, females﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 19]. In this verse there is a refutation of the view of the Thanawiyya (Dualists) that light and darkness are eternal. He used the singular "light" to indicate the category, and because the darkness of each thing varies with the variation of that thing: compare the darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of a dark place; each of them differs from the others. Light, however, is one kind and does not vary as darknesses vary. He mentioned the darknesses first because of his saying, may blessings and peace be upon him: "Allah created His creation in darkness, then sprinkled upon them of His light; whoever is struck by that light is guided, and whoever misses it goes astray."

﴿Then those who disbelieve﴾ after this clarification ﴿ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ they make the idols equal to Him. You say: "I equated this with that," meaning: I made this equal to that. The bāʾ in "bi-Rabbihim" is attached to 'adl (ascribe equals), not to kufr (disbelief). Or: ﴿Then those who disbelieve in their Lord (p-490) turn away﴾ from Him, that is, they turn away from Him; in that case the bāʾ is attached to kufr, and the complement of ya'dilūn, namely "ʿanhu" (from Him), is omitted. The phrase ﴿Then those who disbelieve﴾ is coordinated with "Praise be to Allah," with the meaning: Allah is deserving of praise for what He created, because He created it only as a blessing, and then those who disbelieve in Him turn away, thereby denying His blessing. Or it is coordinated with "created the heavens," with the meaning: He created what He created, things no one other than Him can create, and then they ascribe to Him equals that have no power over any part of it. The word "then" (thumma) signifies the improbability that they would ascribe equals to Him after the clarity of the signs of His power.

He is the One who created you from clay. "Min" (مِن) here denotes the starting point (li-ibtida' al-ghaya, "to indicate the origin"). That is, He began the creation of your origin, meaning Adam, from it.

﴿Then He decreed a term﴾: that is, He determined the term of death.

﴿And a specified term is with Him﴾: this is the term of the Resurrection (ajal al-qiyama).

Alternatively, the first term is the period between one's creation and one's death, and the second is the period between death and resurrection, which is the barzakh (the intermediate state). Or the first term is sleep, and the second is death. Or the second is the same as the first, and its sense is: "and" it is "a specified term," meaning known. Here "ajal musamma" is the subject (mubtada', the subject of a nominal sentence), and the predicate (khabar) is "'indahu" (with Him). The subject has been placed first, though it is indefinite (nakira) and the predicate is an adverbial phrase (zarf), and its proper place is later, because it has been specified by a qualifier and so has come close to being definite (ma'rifa).

﴿Yet you still doubt﴾: tamtarun (تَمْتَرُونَ) means you doubt, from al-miriya (المِرْيَة, doubt), or you dispute, from al-mira' (المِراء, disputation).

The meaning of "thumma" (ثُمَّ, "then/yet") here is to express the improbability that they would doubt it after it has been established that He is the one who gives them life, causes them to die, and raises them.

﴿وَهُوَ اللهُ﴾ is a subject (mubtada') and predicate (khabar) (mubtada' and khabar: the subject and the predicate of a nominal sentence). ﴿فِي السَماواتِ وفي الأرْضِ﴾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) in meaning to the name Allah. It is as if it were said: He is the one worshipped in both. This is like His saying: ﴿And He is the One who is God in the heaven and God on the earth﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 84]. Or [it means]: He is the one known for divinity in both. Or: He is the one who is called Allah in both. The first [view] is based on the premise that the name is derived (mushtaqq), while the others are based on it being non-derived.

﴿يَعْلَمُ سِرَّكم وجَهْرَكُمْ﴾ is a predicate after a predicate, or an independent statement (kalam mubtada'), meaning: He is the one who ﴿knows your secret and your open [speech]﴾ ﴿and knows what you earn﴾ of good and evil, and rewards for it, and punishes.

The "min" in ﴿وَما تَأْتِيهِمْ مِن آيَةٍ﴾ is for totality (istighrab), and the "min" in ﴿مِن آياتِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ is for partitive meaning (tab'id), meaning: no proof ever becomes manifest to them from among the proofs that require reflection and consideration, ﴿إلا كانُوا عَنْها مُعْرِضِينَ﴾ "except that they were turning away from it," neglecting reflection, not paying it any attention, because of the scarcity of their fear and their contemplation of the outcomes.

**Verse 5:** ﴿فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوا﴾ ("Indeed they have denied") is linked to an omitted clause, as if it were said: "If they turn away from the signs, [then] ﴿they have indeed denied﴾ ﴿the truth when it came to them﴾," meaning: with that which is the greatest and most magnificent of signs, namely the Qur'an, with which they were challenged (tahaddi), and regarding which they were unable (fa-ajazu 'anhu).

﴿So there will come to them the news of that which they used to mock﴾, i.e., the news (anba') of the thing at which they used to mock, which is the Qur'an; that is, its reports and its circumstances. The meaning is: they will know what they mocked at. That will be at the time of the sending down of punishment upon them in this world, or on the Day of Resurrection, or at the manifestation of Islam and the exaltation of its word (ulluw kalimatihi).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 6:

﴿Did they not see﴾ meaning: the deniers. ﴿How many generations (qarn) did We destroy before them?﴾ The qarn is the span of time in which the people of one era pass away, and it is eighty years, or seventy. ﴿We had established them﴾ is in the place of a genitive (jarr) as a description of "qarn," and it was put in the plural according to the meaning. ﴿On the earth in a way We have not established for you.﴾ Tamkin (establishment) in the lands is the giving of power (al-mukna), and the meaning is: We did not give the people of Makkah anything like what We gave ʿAd, Thamud and others of physical stature and expansiveness, in wealth, and in support through the means of this world. ﴿And We sent the sky﴾ meaning the rain.

﴿Upon them in abundant (midrar) measure﴾ meaning plentiful, and it is a circumstantial clause (hal) from "the sky." ﴿And We made the rivers flow beneath them﴾ beneath their trees. The meaning is: they lived in fertility, among rivers and fruits, and the watering of abundant rain. ﴿Then We destroyed them for their sins﴾ and that did not avail them anything. ﴿And We brought into being after them another generation﴾ as a replacement for them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 7:

﴿Had We sent down to you a book written﴾ on ﴿paper﴾, meaning on a sheet, ﴿and they had touched it with their hands﴾. The phrase ﴿with their hands﴾ is ﴿هو لِلتَّأْكِيدِ﴾ (li-l-ta'kid, for emphasis), ﴿lest they say: "Our eyes have only been dazzled"﴾ [al-Hijr: 15]. Among those who serve as proof against them are the blind.

﴿Those who disbelieved would have said: "This is nothing but manifest magic"﴾, out of obstinacy and stubborn opposition to the truth after its manifestation.

(p-492) ﴿And they say, "Why has not a angel been sent down upon him?"﴾ — why not (halla) — ﴿upon him﴾ — upon the Prophet (ﷺ) — ﴿an angel﴾ who would speak to us, [declaring] that he is a prophet. So Allah said: ﴿And if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decreed﴾ — the matter of their destruction would have been decreed — ﴿and then they would not be reprieved﴾ — they would not be given respite even for the blink of an eye after its descent, because when they witnessed an angel in his true form, their souls would depart from the terror of what they were witnessing.

The meaning of "then" (thumma) is the distance between the two matters: the decreeing of the matter and the non-reprieve. He made the non-reprieve more severe than the decreeing of the matter, because the sudden arrival of hardship is more severe than the hardship itself.

"﴿And if We had made him an angel﴾: and if We had made the Messenger an angel, as they proposed. For they used to say at one time: "Why has an angel not been sent down to Muhammad?" and at another time they would say: "This is only a human being like you." And had our Lord willed, He would have sent down angels.

﴿We would have made him a man﴾: We would have sent him in the form of a man, just as Jibril (peace be upon him) used to descend upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the most common circumstances in the form of Dihya. For they would not remain [able to bear] seeing angels in their own forms.

﴿And We would have confused for them what they confuse﴾: We would have mixed up for them and made it ambiguous regarding his matter, since his course would be like your course, O Muhammad. For they would say, when they saw the angel in the form of a human: "This is a human being, not an angel." It is said: "I covered the matter over the people (labastu al-amr 'ala al-qawm), and I made it obscure (albastuhu)" when you resemble it and make it ambiguous for them (ashkaltahu 'alayhim)."

Then He consoled His Prophet regarding the mockery he suffered from his people, by His saying: ﴿And indeed, messengers before you were mocked, but those who ridiculed them were encompassed by that which they used to mock.﴾ So the thing they used to mock encompassed them, namely the truth, since they were destroyed on account of their mockery of it. And "minhum" (from them) is connected to "sakhiru" (ridiculed), like His saying: ﴿So they mock them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 79]. The pronoun refers to the messengers. The dal is kasra according to Abu 'Amr and 'Asim, due to the meeting of two unvowelled letters (iltiqa' al-sakinayn), while the others read it with damma, following the damma of the ta' (in "usti-hziʾa" → "ustuhzi'a").

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 11:

﴿Say: Travel through the earth, then observe how was the end of those who denied.﴾ The difference between "fa-unzuru" (fa-nẓurū, "so observe") and "thumma unzuru" (thumma nẓurū, "then observe") is that in "fa-unẓurū" observing is made a consequence of travelling, as if it were said: "Travel in order to observe, and do not travel the travel of the heedless." The meaning of "Travel through the earth, then observe" is the permissibility of travelling through the earth for trade and other purposes, and the obligation of observing the traces of those who perished. He drew attention to this with "thumma" (then), because of the distance between what is obligatory and what is permissible.

﴿قُلْ لِمَن ما في السَماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾ "مَن" اسْتِفْهامٌ (interrogative), و"ما" بِمَعْنى الَّذِي (meaning "that which") في مَوْضِعِ الرَفْعِ عَلى الِابْتِداءِ (in the nominative position as the subject of a nominal sentence), و"لِمَن" خَبَرُهُ (its predicate).

﴿قُلْ لِلَّهِ﴾ تَقْرِيرٌ لَهُمْ (a confirmation to them), أيْ: هو لِلَّهِ لا خِلافَ بَيْنِي وبَيْنَكُمْ، ولا تَقْدِرُونَ أنْ تُضِيفُوا مِنهُ شَيْئًا إلى غَيْرِهِ. That is: it belongs to God, there is no disagreement between me and you, and you cannot attribute any part of it to anyone else.

﴿كَتَبَ عَلى نَفْسِهِ الرَحْمَةَ﴾ أصْلُ كَتَبَ: أوْجَبَ (the basic meaning of kataba is "he obligated"), ولَكِنْ لا يَجُوزُ الإجْراءُ عَلى ظاهِرِهِ، إذْ لا يَجِبُ عَلى اللهِ شَيْءٌ لِلْعَبْدِ، فالمُرادُ بِهِ: أنَّهُ وعَدَ ذَلِكَ وعْدًا مُؤَكِّدًا، وهو مُنْجِزُهُ لا مَحالَةَ، وذَكَرَ النَفْسَ لِلِاخْتِصاصِ، ورَفْعِ الوَسائِطِ، ثُمَّ أوْعَدَهم عَلى إغْفالِهِمُ النَظَرَ، وإشْراكِهِمْ بِهِ مَن لا يَقْدِرُ عَلى خَلْقِ شَيْءٍ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿لَيَجْمَعَنَّكم إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ﴾ فَيُجازِيكم عَلى إشْراكِكم. The literal sense of "he obligated" cannot be taken, since nothing is obligatory upon God toward the servant; the intended meaning is that He promised this with an emphatic promise, and He will certainly fulfill it. He mentioned "the self" (nafs) to indicate exclusivity and the removal of intermediaries. Then He threatened them for their neglect of reflection and for associating with Him those who cannot create anything, with His words: ﴿He will surely gather you on the Day of Resurrection﴾, so that He may requite you for your associating others with Him.

﴿لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾ في اليَوْمِ، أوْ في الجَمْعِ. There is no doubt about it: concerning the Day, or concerning the gathering.

﴿الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ نَصْبٌ عَلى الذَمِّ (accusative of dispraise), أيْ: أُرِيدُ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أنْفُسَهم بِاخْتِيارِهِمُ الكُفْرَ ﴿فَهم لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ That is: I mean those who lost their own selves by choosing disbelief, ﴿so they do not believe﴾. وقالَ الأخْفَشُ (al-Akhfash said): "الَّذِينَ" بَدَلٌ مِن "كُمْ" في "لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ" أيْ: لِيَجْمَعَنَّ هَؤُلاءِ المُشْرِكِينَ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أنْفُسَهُمْ، والوَجْهُ هو الأوَّلُ، لِأنَّ سِيبَوَيْهِ (Sibawayh) قالَ: لا يَجُوزُ مَرَرْتَ بِيَ المِسْكِينِ، ولا بِكَ المِسْكِينِ، فَتَجْعَلُ المِسْكِينَ بَدَلًا مِنَ الياءِ، أوِ الكافِ، لِأنَّهُما في غايَةِ الوُضُوحِ، فَلا يَحْتاجانِ إلى البَدَلِ والتَفْسِيرِ. "Those who" is a substitute for "you" in "He will surely gather you": that is, He will surely gather these polytheists who lost their selves. But the first view is the correct one, because Sibawayh said: it is not permitted to say "marartu bi al-miskin" (I passed by me, the poor one) nor "bika al-miskin" (by you, the poor one), so that you make "al-miskin" a substitute for the ya' or the kaf, because these two are entirely clear and therefore do not need a substitute or an explanation.

ﷺ

﴿And to Him belongs﴾ is a conjunction (ʿaṭf) on "lillāh" (to Allah). ﴿whatever dwells (sakana) in the night and the day﴾ — from al-sukhnā (dwelling, residing), so that it encompasses both the one that dwells and the one that moves. Or it is from al-sukūn (stillness), and its meaning is: whatever is still and whatever moves within them. He has been content with one of the two opposites over the other, as in His saying: ﴿that protects you from the heat﴾ [al-Naḥl: 81], meaning: the heat and the cold. He mentioned stillness because it is more common than movement. And this is an argument against the polytheists, for they did not deny that He is the Creator of all and its Manager. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾, who hears (p-494) every thing heard, and knows every thing known, so nothing is hidden from Him of what the two realms (al-malawān, i.e., the night and the day) contain.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 14:

﴿Say: Shall I take as a protector other than Allah⁠﴾, meaning a helper and an object of worship. It is the second object (maf'ul thani) of "atakhidh" (I take), and the first is "ghayr" (other than). He placed the interrogative hamza before the object of "atakhidh" rather than before the verb itself, because the denial concerns taking something other than Allah as a protector, not taking a protector in general; therefore it deserved to be placed first.

﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, in the genitive (bi'l-jarr), is an attribute of Allah, meaning its innovator and creator. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father): "I did not know the meaning of fatir (originator) until two Bedouins came to me disputing over a well, and one of them said: 'I am the one who fatartuha (originated it),' i.e., I began it."

﴿And He feeds and is not fed﴾, i.e., He provides sustenance and is not provided for; all benefits come from Him, and benefiting from anything is not permissible for Him. ﴿Say: Indeed I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit﴾, because the Prophet precedes his community in Islam, as in His saying: ﴿And I have been commanded to this, and I am the first of the Muslims﴾ [al-An'am: 163]. ﴿And do not be among the polytheists﴾. And it was said to me: "Do not be among the polytheists." Had it been conjoined grammatically to what precedes it, it would have been said: "wa-alla akuna" (and that I not be). The meaning: I have been commanded to submit (to Islam) and forbidden from associating partners with Allah.

"Say: Indeed I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great day." That is: "Indeed I fear the punishment of a great day, which is the Resurrection, if I disobey my Lord." So the conditional clause is interposed between the agent and the object, and its answer is omitted.

"Whoever is turned away from it (the punishment) on that Day, then He has had mercy on him" (﴿مَن يُصْرَفْ عَنْهُ﴾ ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ فَقَدْ رَحِمَهُ﴾): that is, Allah has granted him the greatest mercy, which is evident salvation. (Reading "مَن يَصْرِفْ" with the vowel on the verb is transmitted from Hamzah, ʿAlī, and Abū Bakr), meaning: whoever Allah turns the punishment away from. ﴿And that is the clear triumph﴾.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 17:

﴿And if Allah touches you with harm﴾, [that is] from sickness, or poverty, or other of His afflictions (p-495), ﴿there is no remover of it except Him﴾, meaning: there is no one able to remove it except Him. ﴿And if He touches you with good﴾, [that is] from wealth or health, ﴿then He is over all things Competent﴾, meaning: He is able to sustain it and to take it away.

Translation:

﴿And He is the Subduer﴾ is a subject and predicate, meaning: the Victorious, the Omnipotent, ﴿over His servants﴾ is a predicate following a predicate, meaning: exalted over them by power. Al-qahr (subjugation) is the attainment of one's purpose by preventing others from attaining theirs. ﴿And He is the All-Wise﴾ in carrying out His purpose, ﴿the All-Aware﴾ of those who are subdued among His servants.

﴿Say: "What thing is greatest as a witness?"﴾ "Ayyu shay'" (what thing) is the subject (mubtada', the grammatical subject), "akbaru" (greatest) is its predicate (khabar), and "shahadatan" (as a witness) is a specification (tamyiz, an accusative noun clarifying the sense of the predicate). "Ayyu" is a word used to refer to some part of what it is annexed to. When it is interrogative, its answer is named by the noun to which it is annexed. His saying ﴿Say: "God"﴾ is the answer, meaning: God is the greatest as a witness. So "Allah" is the subject, and the predicate is omitted. This is evidence that it is permissible to apply the name "thing" (shay') to God, Exalted is He, because "thing" is a name for that which exists, and is not applied to that which does not exist. God, Exalted is He, exists, so He is a thing. Therefore we say: God, Exalted is He, is a thing, unlike other things. Then he begins: ﴿He is a witness between me and you﴾, meaning: He is a witness between me and you. It is also possible that the answer is ﴿God is a witness between me and you﴾, because if God is a witness between him and them, then the greatest thing as a witness is one who is a witness for him.

﴿And this Qur'an has been revealed to me so that I may warn you thereby, and whoever it reaches﴾, meaning: and whoever the Qur'an has reached until the Hour arrives. In the hadith: "Whoever the Qur'an has reached is as if he has seen Muhammad (ﷺ)." The word "man" (whoever) is in the accusative position by conjunction (ʿatf) upon "kum" (you). What is intended by it is the people of Makkah. The returning pronoun referring to it is omitted, meaning: whoever it (the Qur'an) has reached. The doer of "balagha" (reached) is the pronoun referring to the Qur'an.

﴿Do you really bear witness that there are other gods with God?﴾ This is an interrogative of denial and rebuke. ﴿Say: "I do not bear witness"﴾ to what you bear witness to. He repeated "say" for emphasis. ﴿Indeed He is only one God﴾. The "ma" is a particle (kaffah) that cancels the governing power of "inna" (indeed) so it no longer governs. "Huwa" (He) is the subject, "ilah" (god) is its predicate, and "wahid" (one) is an adjective. Or "ma" has the meaning of "alladhi" (the one who), in the accusative position as the object of "inna", "huwa" is the subject, "ilah" is its predicate, and the clause is the relative clause (silah) of "alladhi", and "wahid" is the predicate of "inna". This second view is more fitting. ﴿And indeed I am free from what you associate with Him﴾.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 20:

﴿Those to whom We have given the Book﴾ means: the Jews and the Christians. "The Book" refers to the Torah (al-Tawrah) and the Gospel (al-Injil).

﴿They recognize him﴾, i.e., the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), by his physical description (ḥilyah) and his attributes (naʿt) that are established in the two Books.

﴿As they recognize their own sons﴾ by their features (ḥilan) and their characteristics (nuʿūt). This is an argument addressed to the people of Makkah, pointing to the People of the Book's knowledge of him and to the truth of his prophethood. Then He said: ﴿Those who have lost their souls﴾, from among the polytheists and from among the People of the Book who deny, ﴿they do not believe﴾ in him.

"And who is more unjust than one who fabricates against Allah a lie" — ﴿وَمَن أظْلَمُ﴾ is an interrogative (istifham) that carries the sense of negation, i.e., no one is more unjust to his own self. Injustice (al-zulm, ظلم) is placing a thing in other than its proper place, and the most grievous of it is taking a created being as a deity.

﴿مِمَّنِ افْتَرى﴾ (ifterā) means he invented or fabricated (ikhtalaqa),

﴿عَلى اللهِ كَذِبًا﴾ "against Allah a lie," so that he describes Him with what is not befitting to Him, ﴿أوْ كَذَّبَ بِآياتِهِ﴾ "or denies His signs," meaning the Qur'an and the miracles (al-mu'jizat).

﴿إنَّهُ﴾ indeed (inna) it is the matter and the affair (al-amr wa al-sha'n) ﴿لا يُفْلِحُ الظالِمُونَ﴾ "that the wrongdoers will not succeed." They combined two false matters: they lied against Allah concerning what has no proof for it, and they denied what had been established by proof, when they said: "The angels are the daughters of Allah," and they named the Qur'an and the miracles "magic."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 22:

﴿And [remember] the Day We gather them all together⦆ is an object (maf'ul bihi), and the implied sense is: "And [mention] the day We gather them."

﴿Jamee'an⦆ (all together) is a circumstantial qualifier (hal) referring back to the pronoun of the object. ﴿Then We will say to those who associated [partners]⦆ with Allah, others besides Him, as a rebuke. The verb "naqulu" with the ya' (yā', i.e., "yaqulu") in both places is the reading of Ya'qub.

﴿Where are your partners⦆: your gods which you made partners of Allah, ﴿whom you used to claim⦆, i.e., you used to claim them to be partners; the two objects have been omitted.

﴿Then there will not be﴾. With the ya' (يَكُن, "there will not be" with a masculine verb form instead of the feminine tā'), read by Ḥamza and ʿAlī.

﴿their trial﴾ meaning their disbelief, ﴿except that they said: "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾. He means: then the outcome of their disbelief, to which they held firm for their whole lives and fought for, will not be anything but denying it, disowning it, and swearing that they had no connection with following it. Or [the meaning is]: then their answer will not be anything but that they said. It was called a trial (fitna) because it is a lie.

With raising of fitna (فِتْنَتُهُمْ as the subject), read by Makkī, the Syrian reader (Shāmī), and Ḥafs. Whoever reads (تَكُنْ) with the tā' and the raised fitna has made fitna the subject (ism) of takun, and "an qālū" (أنْ قالُوا, "that they said") the predicate (khabar). That is: their trial will not be anything but their statement. Whoever reads with the ya' and the accusative fitna (فِتْنَةَ) has taken it as the object, referring to the statement (al-maqāla).

(رَبَّنا) "Our Lord" is read in the vocative by Ḥamza and ʿAlī, meaning "O our Lord." The others read it in the genitive, as a qualifier (na't, adjective) of the name of Allah.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 24:

﴿Look﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿how they lied against themselves﴾ by their saying: "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."

Mujahid said: When Allah gathers the creatures, and the polytheists see the vastness of Allah's mercy and the intercession of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for the believers, some of them say to others: "Come, let us conceal our polytheism, so that perhaps we may be saved along with the people of monotheism (tawhid)." Then Allah says to them: ﴿Where are your associates whom you used to claim?﴾ [al-An'am: 22]. They say: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23]. Then Allah sets a seal upon their mouths, and their limbs bear witness against them.

﴿And what they used to fabricate will be lost to them﴾, meaning: what they used to fabricate, namely His divinity and His intercession, will be absent from them and lost to them.

﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾ while you recite the Qur'an. It is related that Abu Sufyan, al-Walid, al-Nadr, and their like gathered to listen to the recitation of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They said to al-Nadr, "What is Muhammad saying?" He replied, "By Allah, I do not know what Muhammad is saying, except that he moves his tongue and says, 'the fables of the ancients,' like what I have told you about the past generations." Abu Sufyan said, "I think it is true." Abu Jahl said, "No indeed." Then it was revealed: ﴿And We have placed over their hearts veils﴾, meaning coverings (akinna, plural of kinan), which is the covering, like inan and a'inna.

﴿Lest they understand it﴾ means "out of aversion to their understanding it." ﴿And in their ears is deafness﴾ means a heaviness that prevents hearing. The word waqr is in the singular because it is a verbal noun (masdar). It is coordinated with akinna. This is a proof for us against the Mu'tazila (the rationalist school) regarding al-aslah (what is most beneficial or optimal).

﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it, until, when they come to you disputing with you, those who disbelieve say...﴾ The particle hatta (حتى) is the one after which sentences occur, and the sentence is his statement: (idha ja'uka... yaqulu alladhina kafaru) "when they come to you... those who disbelieve say." The phrase yujadilunaka (﴿disputing with you﴾) is in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal). It is also permissible for hatta to be a preposition, in which case idha ja'uka (﴿when they come to you﴾) is in a genitive position, meaning "up to the time of their coming." Yujadilunaka is then a circumstantial clause, and yaqulu alladhina kafaru (﴿those who disbelieve say﴾) is an explanation of it. The meaning is that their denial of the signs reached the point that they dispute with you and deny you. Their disputing is explained by their saying: ﴿This is nothing but the fables of the ancients﴾, that is, the Qur'an is nothing but fables, thereby making the speech of Allah into falsehoods. The singular of asatir (fables) is ustura.

﴿And they﴾ i.e., the polytheists, ﴿forbid others from it﴾, forbidding people from the Qur'an, or from the Messenger and his followers, and from believing in him, ﴿and keep away from it﴾, keeping themselves far from it, so they go astray and lead others astray.

﴿And they destroy only themselves, yet they perceive it not﴾, meaning the harm does not extend beyond them to others, even though they think they are harming the Messenger of Allah. It was also said that Abu Talib was meant by this, because he used to forbid the Quraysh from harming the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), yet he kept away from him and did not believe in him; but the first view is more fitting.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 27:**

﴿And if you could see﴾: its answer (jawab) has been omitted, meaning: "And if you could see, you would witness a tremendous matter" ﴿when they are made to stand before the Fire﴾, either so that they are shown it and see it directly, or they are detained on the Path (al-Sirat) above the Fire. ﴿They will say, "Oh, would that we were returned"﴾ to the worldly life. They wished for a return to the worldly life so that they might believe. Their wish is complete here, and then they begin with His words: ﴿and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers﴾, as promisers of faith, as if they had said: "We would not deny, and we would believe."

(﴿وَلا نُكَذِّبَ﴾، ﴿وَنَكُونَ﴾) Hamzah, Ali, and Hafs read these with the accusative, as an answer to the wish (al-tamanni, "wish") with the conjunction waw and with the particle "an" implied. Its meaning is: "If we are returned, we will not deny, and we will be among the believers." Al-Shami agreed with them on ﴿وَنَكُونَ﴾.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 28:

﴿Nay(bal)﴾ is for the turning away (al-idrab) from fulfilling what they wished for. ﴿It became evident to them﴾, i.e., appeared to them, ﴿what they used to conceal﴾ from people ﴿before﴾ in the world, of their ugly deeds and disgraceful acts recorded in their scrolls.

It is said: this refers to the hypocrites, and that their hypocrisy which they used to keep secret will become apparent. Or it refers to the People of the Book, and that there will become apparent to them what they used to conceal of the truth of the prophethood of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). ﴿And if they were returned﴾ to the world after standing before the Fire, ﴿they would return to what they were forbidden﴾ of disbelief, ﴿and indeed they are liars﴾ regarding what they promised of themselves, for they would not keep it.

"And they say" is coordinated with "they would have returned" (lacadu): that is, even if they were returned, they would have disbelieved, and they would have said: "There is nothing but our life of this world" (in ʿālam al-dunyā), as they used to say before witnessing the Resurrection [or it is coordinated with His saying: "And indeed they are liars," meaning: indeed they are a people who lie in everything, and they are the ones who said: "There is nothing but our life of this world"]. And "hiya" (it) is a pronoun referring to life (kināya ʿan al-ḥayāh), or it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa): "There is nothing but our life of this world, and we will not be resurrected."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 30:

﴿And if you could see when they are made to stand before their Lord﴾. It is a metaphor for being detained for rebuke and questioning, just as a guilty slave is made to stand before his master so that he may punish him. Or it means they are made to stand before the requital of their Lord. ﴿He will say﴾ is an answer to an implied question, as if it were said: "What will their Lord say to them when they are made to stand before Him?" So it is said: He will say: ﴿Is this not the truth?﴾, that is, the Resurrection, ﴿the truth﴾, meaning the thing that exists and is real. This is a rebuke to them for denying the Resurrection, and for their saying, concerning what they used to hear about the Resurrection: "It is not the truth." ﴿They will say: Yes, by our Lord!﴾ They acknowledged it, and confirmed the acknowledgment with an oath. ﴿He will say﴾ God Most High says: ﴿So taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve﴾, that is, because of your disbelief.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 31:

﴿Those who denied the meeting with Allah have indeed lost﴾, meaning by reaching the Hereafter and what is connected to it. Or it is left to its apparent meaning, because one who denies the Resurrection denies the vision (of Allah). ﴿Until﴾ is an extent (ghaya) of "denied," not of "lost," because their loss has no end. ﴿When the Hour comes upon them﴾, that is: the Resurrection, because the period of its delay, given the eternity of what follows it, is like a single hour,

﴿suddenly﴾, meaning unexpectedly. Its being in the accusative is either as a circumstantial state (hal), meaning "surprising," or as a verbal noun (masdar), as if it were said: "The Hour surprised them with a surprise," and it is the arrival of a thing upon its owner without his knowing its time. ﴿They will say: "Oh, our regret"﴾: this is a call of lamentation, its meaning being: "O regret, come forth, for this is your time." ﴿For what we neglected﴾, meaning fell short, ﴿concerning it﴾, in the life of this world, or concerning the Hour, that is, we fell short in regard to its affair and in believing in it. ﴿While they bear their burdens﴾, their sins, ﴿upon their backs﴾. He specified the back because the customary way of carrying loads is upon the backs, just as earning is customarily done by the hands. This is a metaphor for being bound to them in a way that never leaves them. It was also said: when the disbeliever comes out of his grave, he will be met by the ugliest of forms and the foulest of smells, and he will say: "I am your evil deed. You rode me many times in the world, and today I ride you." ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they bear﴾: how wretched is the thing they carry. The particle "unquestionably" (ala) conveys the magnification of what is mentioned after it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 32:

﴿And the life of this world is nothing but play and amusement.﴾ It is an answer to their saying: ﴿There is nothing but our life of this world.﴾ [al-An'am: 29]. Al-La'ib (play): leaving what benefits for what does not benefit. Al-Lahw (amusement): inclining away from seriousness toward frivolity. It has been said: the people of the life of this world are only people of play and amusement. And it has been said: the deeds of the life of this world are only play and amusement, because they do not produce any benefit, whereas the deeds of the Hereafter produce great benefits. ﴿And the abode of the Hereafter﴾: "al-dar" is the subject (mubtada'), and "al-akhirah" is its attribute (sifah). (Wa-ladar al-akhirah) with the idafah (construct form) is the reading of Ibn 'Amir (Shami), meaning: and the abode of the final Hour, because a thing is not added to its own attribute. The predicate (khabar) of the subject, according to both readings, is ﴿better for those who are God-conscious.﴾ In this is evidence that everything other than the deeds of the God-conscious is play and amusement. (Afala ta'qilun) with the ta' (you) is the reading of Ibn Kathir (Madani) and Hafs.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 33:

When Abu Jahl said: "We do not deny you, O Muhammad! Indeed you are, in our eyes, truthful. What we deny is what you have brought to us," the verse was revealed: ﴿We know indeed that it grieves you what they say﴾, where the ha' (in innahu) is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-sha'n), ﴿but it is not you they deny﴾, meaning they do not attribute lying to you.

With the light (takhfif) reading, Nafi' and Ali read it as "yukdhibunaka," from akdhabahu, meaning: when one finds him to be a liar.

﴿But the wrongdoers deny the signs of God﴾. This is the placing of the apparent noun in the position of the pronoun (iqamat al-zahir maqam al-mudmar). It indicates that they wronged themselves in their denial. The bā' (in bi-āyāti) is related either to "yajhadūn" or to "al-ẓālimīn," as in His saying: ﴿So they wronged themselves by them﴾ [al-A'raf: 103]. The meaning is: your denial is a matter that returns to God, because you are His Messenger, who confirms the miracles; so they do not in reality deny you, but rather they deny God, since denying the Messenger is denying the One who sent him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 34:

﴿And indeed, messengers were denied before you﴾ — a consolation for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It is also evidence that His saying: ﴿So they do not deny you﴾ is not a negation of their denial of him. Rather, it is like your saying to your servant boy when some people insult him: "They have not insulted you; rather, they have insulted me."

﴿So they were patient﴾ — patience (al-sabr) is restraining the self in the face of what is disliked, ﴿over what they were denied and harmed﴾, over their denial and their harming.

﴿Until Our help came to them, and none can alter the words of Allah﴾ — His promises, from His saying: ﴿And certainly Our word had preceded to Our servants, the messengers, that they would indeed be helped﴾ [al-Saffat: 171–172], and ﴿Indeed, We will help Our messengers﴾ [Ghafir: 51].

﴿And certainly there has come to you some of the news of the messengers﴾ — some of their reports and stories, and what they endured of the perseverance against the polytheists. Al-Akhfash permitted that "min" (some of) be extra (ziyadah), with "the news of the messengers" as the subject (al-fa'il). Sibawayh does not permit its being extra in an affirmative (wajib) sentence.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 35:

It was hard for the Prophet (ﷺ) that his people disbelieved and turned away, and he would love the coming of signs so that they would become Muslim. So it was revealed: ﴿And if their turning away is hard on you﴾ — it became great and burdensome — ﴿their turning away﴾ from Islam. ﴿Then if you are able to seek a tunnel﴾ — an opening through which you could pass into what is beneath the earth — ﴿in the earth﴾ is a description of "a tunnel," ﴿or a ladder into the sky, and bring them a sign﴾ from it — ﴿then do so.﴾ This is the answer to ﴿If you are able﴾. And if you are able, its answer is the answer of ﴿And if their turning away is hard﴾. The meaning is: you are not able to do that. The purpose is to show his eagerness for the Islam of his people, and that if he were able to bring them a sign from beneath the earth or from above the sky, he would bring it, hoping for their faith. ﴿And if God had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance﴾ — He would have made them such that they choose guidance. But since He knew that they choose disbelief, He did not will to gather them upon that. So said the Shaykh Abu Mansur, may God have mercy on him. ﴿So do not be among the ignorant﴾ — among those who are ignorant of this.

Then He informed that his eagerness for their guidance is of no benefit, since they do not hear, being like the dead, by His saying: ﴿Only those who hear respond﴾. That is: only those who hear your call with their hearts respond to your call. ﴿And the dead﴾ is the subject (mubtada'), meaning: the disbelievers.

﴿Allah will raise them up, then to Him they will be returned﴾. Then they will hear, but before that they will not.

"They say: Why was a sign not sent down to him from his Lord?" That is: why was it not sent down upon him? ﴿A sign from his Lord﴾, such as what they propose: turning the Safa into gold, widening the land of Makkah, and making rivers flow through it. ﴿Say: Indeed, Allah is able to send down a sign﴾ as they have proposed. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾: that Allah is able to send down that sign; or they do not know the trial that would be upon them in the sign if it were sent down.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 38:**

﴿And there is no creature (dābba) on the earth﴾ — dābba is a noun for that which crawls (yadibbu), and it applies to both the masculine and the feminine. ﴿On the earth﴾ — in the place of a genitive (jarr), it is an adjectival qualifier of dābba. ﴿Nor any bird that flies with its two wings﴾ — he restricted the flying to "with its two wings" in order to negate the metaphorical usage, because of what is said of other than a bird: "ṭāra" (it flew), when it hastens.

﴿Except that they are communities like you﴾ — in creation, death, resurrection, and need for a manager (mudabbir) who directs the affairs of their proper conduct. ﴿We have not neglected﴾ — we have not left out ﴿in the Book﴾ — in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawḥ al-maḥfūẓ) ﴿anything﴾ — of that; we did not write it down, and we did not record what was necessary to be recorded. Or "the Book" means the Qur'an. His words ﴿anything﴾ mean: anything they need, so it comprises what He has obligated us to worship by explicit expression (ʿibāra), allusion (ishāra), implication (dalāla), and necessary inference (iqtiḍāʾ).

﴿Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾ — meaning all the communities of the creatures and the birds; so He will settle the dispute between one of them and another, as has been narrated: that He will take retribution for the hornless (jammāʾ) from the horned (qarnāʾ), and then He will say: "Be dust." And the reason He said "communities" (umam) despite the singular forms dābba and ṭāʾir is for the sense of comprehensiveness (istighrāq) in both of them.

When He had mentioned, from among His creatures and the signs of His power, what bears witness to His lordship and calls out to His greatness, He said: ﴿Those who deny Our signs are deaf﴾, not hearing the words of the one who admonishes, ﴿and dumb﴾, not speaking the truth, floundering ﴿in darknesses﴾, that is, in the darkness of ignorance, bewilderment and disbelief, heedless of pondering over that and reflecting upon it. ﴿Deaf and dumb﴾ is the predicate of "those who", and the entry of the conjunction "wa" does not prevent this. And ﴿in darknesses﴾ is another predicate. Then He said, as a notification that He is one who does whatever He wills: ﴿Whomever Allah wills to lead astray, He leads astray﴾, that is, whomever Allah wills to be led astray, He leads astray, ﴿and whomever He wills, He places upon a straight path﴾. In this is an indication of the createdness of acts (khalq al-af'al), of the will for sins (iradat al-ma'asi), and of the negation of what is best (nafy al-aslah).

﴿Say: Have you considered?﴾ With the softening of the hamza (*talyīn al-hamza*, pronouncing it as an intermediate sound): Madani; without softening it: ʿAlī. Its meaning is: "Do you know that the matter is as you are told? Then inform me of what you have." The second pronoun (*al-ḍamīr al-thānī*) has no place in the grammatical analysis (*al-iʿrāb*, i'rab, the grammatical parsing of words), and the *tāʾ* (ت) is the pronoun of the subject (*ḍamīr al-fāʿil*). The object of the interrogation (*mutaʿallaq al-istikhbār*) is omitted, and its estimated reading is: "Have you considered [yourselves]﴿if the punishment of God comes upon you, or the Hour comes upon you﴾: whom do you call upon?" Then he rebuked them with His saying: ﴿Other than God do you call upon?﴾ That is: Do you single out your gods for supplication in the matter that is your habit when harm befalls you, or do you call upon God apart from them?! ﴿If you are truthful﴾ in your claim that the idols are gods, then call upon them, so that they may deliver you.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 41:

﴿Rather, it is Him you call upon﴾: rather, you single Him out for supplication, to the exclusion of the gods.

﴿So He removes that for which you call upon Him﴾: that is, the affliction which you call upon Him to remove, ﴿if He wills﴾: if He intends to show you favour, ﴿and you forget what you associate﴾: and you abandon your gods, or you do not mention your gods at that time, because your minds are absorbed in the remembrance of your Lord alone, since He is the One able to remove harm and no other.

It is also permissible for the interrogative to be linked to His words, ﴿Other than God will you call upon?﴾, as if it were said: "Tell me, if the punishment of God comes upon you, is it other than God you will call upon?"

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 42:

﴿And We certainly sent [messengers] to communities before you﴾ — [rusulan, "messengers"], so the object is elided. ﴿So they denied them, and We seized them with adversity and hardship﴾ — with misery and harm; or the first [al-ba'sa', "adversity"] is drought and hunger, and the second [al-darra', "hardship"] is sickness and loss of lives and property.

﴿So that they might humble themselves﴾ — they would abase themselves and submit humbly to their Lord, and repent of their sins, for souls become humbled when severe calamities descend.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 43:

﴿Then why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves?﴾ That is: why did they not humble themselves through repentance (tawbah)? Its meaning is the negation of humbling themselves, as if it were said: "They did not humble themselves when Our punishment came to them." But it was expressed with "lawla" (why not / if only... not) to convey that they had no excuse for abandoning humility except their obstinacy. ﴿But their hearts became hardened﴾, so they were not restrained by what they were afflicted with. ﴿And Satan made attractive to them what they were doing﴾, and they became pleased with their deeds, which Satan had made attractive to them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 44:

﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾ of adversity and hardship, that is, they abandoned heeding it and it did not restrain them.

﴿We opened for them the gates of everything﴾ of health, abundance, and all kinds of blessings. (فَتَّحْنا, "We opened" with the doubling of the letter ta', is the reading of Ibn Amir al-Shami.)

﴿Until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given﴾ of good things and blessings.

﴿We seized them suddenly, and then they were in despair﴾ hopeless, grief-stricken. Its root meaning (أصله, asluhu) is lowering the head in sorrow over what has befallen one, or in regret over what has escaped one. And إذا (idha), here, is for sudden occurrence (lil-mufajaah, "for suddenness").

﴿So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off﴾, that is: they were destroyed to the last one, and not one of them was left.

﴿And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾: an announcement that praise of Allah is obligatory when the wrongdoers are destroyed, and that it is among the greatest of blessings and the most abundant of portions. Or it means: praise Allah for destroying those who did not praise Allah.

Then He indicated His power and His oneness by His saying: ﴿Say: "Have you considered, if Allah took away your hearing and your sight"﴾ by making you deaf and blind, ﴿and sealed over your hearts﴾ thus depriving you of intellect and discernment, ﴿what god other than Allah could bring them back to you?﴾ that is, bring back what was taken and sealed over. "Man" is in the nominative case as the subject (mubtada'), "ilah" is its predicate (khabar), "ghayr" is an adjective (sifah) of "ilah," and likewise "ya'tikum" (the verb) is an adjective too, and the clause occupies the position of the two objects of "ara'aytum" (have you considered). The answer to the conditional (jawab al-shart) is omitted.

﴿Look how We vary the signs﴾ for them, ﴿repeating them﴾, ﴿yet they turn away﴾, that is, they turn aside from the signs after they have become manifest. Al-sudud (turning away) means aversion from something.

(p-505)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 47:

﴿Say: Tell Me, if the punishment of Allah should come upon you suddenly﴾ without its signs having appeared, ﴿or openly﴾ with its signs having appeared. And from al-Hasan: at night or by day. ﴿Will any be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?﴾ No one is destroyed with the destruction of punishment and wrath except those who wronged themselves through their disbelief in their Lord.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 48:

﴿We do not send the messengers except as bearers of good news and warners,﴾ with the Gardens and the Fires, to the believers and the disbelievers. We did not send them so that signs would be demanded of them after their matter had become clear through decisive proofs and manifest evidences.

﴿Whoever believes and makes amends,﴾ i.e., persists in his faith, ﴿there is no fear for them, nor shall they grieve.﴾ (فَلا خَوْفَ) is read by Ya'qub (with the fatha on the fa' and the omission of the tanwin, "lā khawfa").

The commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 49:

﴿And those who denied Our signs, the punishment will touch them﴾ The punishment is made to be a toucher (māss), as if it were a living being that does to them whatever pains it wills.

﴿Because they used to defiantly disobey (yafsuqūn)﴾ Because of their defiance (fisq), and their going out of obedience to Allah Most High through disbelief.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 50:

﴿Say: I do not tell you that with me are the treasuries of Allah﴾. That is: His distribution among the creation, and His provisions.

The grammatical position (*maḥall*, the place in the sentence that a word occupies for i'rab, or grammatical analysis) of ﴿and I do not know the unseen﴾ is in the accusative case, as a coordination (*'aṭf*) upon the position of "*'indī khazā'inu Allāh*" (with me are the treasuries of Allah), because it is part of what is said. It is as if he said: "I do not tell you this statement, nor this statement."

﴿Nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾. That is: I do not claim what minds would find unlikely, that a human could possess the treasuries of Allah, or knowledge of the unseen, or a claim of being an angel. I only claim what has been granted to many humans, which is prophethood.

﴿I follow only what is revealed to me﴾. That is: I only inform you of what Allah has sent down to me. ﴿Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?﴾ This is a parable for the one who is astray and the one who is guided, or for the one who follows what is revealed to him and the one who does not follow it, or for the one who claims the straight path, which is prophethood, and the one who claims the impossible, which is divinity.

﴿Will you not then reflect?﴾ That is: do not be astray like the likeness of the blind; or so that you may know that I have not claimed what is unbecoming for a human; or so that you may know that following what is revealed to me is something I cannot do without.

(p-506)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 51:

﴿And warn thereby﴾ with what is revealed (bi-ma yuhā), ﴿those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾. They are the Muslims who affirm the resurrection (al-ba'th), except that they are negligent in action (mufarrituna fi'l-'amal), so he warns them with what has been revealed to him; or they are the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab), because they affirm the resurrection. ﴿They will have, besides Him, no protector and no intercessor﴾. This is in the position of a circumstantial clause (fi mawdi' al-hal) from "yuhsharu", meaning: ﴿who fear that they will be gathered﴾ while not being helped (ghayra mansurin), nor having anyone intercede for them (wa-la mashfu'an lahum). ﴿That they may perhaps fear Allah (la'allahum yattaqun)﴾: they enter the company of the people of taqwa (zumrat ahl al-taqwa).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 52:

When He commanded the Prophet ﷺ to warn those who are not God-conscious, so that they might become God-conscious, He then commanded him to draw near to the God-conscious and forbade him from driving them away: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord at dawn and dusk﴾. He praised them for persisting in calling upon their Lord, meaning worshipping Him, and for being constant in it. The mention of dawn and dusk is intended to signify continuity, or its meaning is: they perform the Dawn prayer and the Afternoon prayer, or the five prayers. (bil-ghudwah) is the reading of the Syrian (Shami) reader. He described them as sincere in their worship by His saying: ﴿seeking His Face﴾. The "face" is used to express the essence and reality of a thing.

It was revealed concerning the poor: Bilal, Suhayb, Ammar and their like, when the leaders of the polytheists said: "If you drive away these riffraff, we will sit with you." The Prophet ﷺ said: "I am not one to drive away the believers." They said: "Make for us a day and for them a day," and they sought a written agreement in this regard. So he called Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, to write it. Then the poor stood up and sat in a corner, and this verse was revealed. The Prophet ﷺ threw down the document, went to the poor, and embraced them.

﴿There is nothing of their reckoning upon you﴾ is like His saying: ﴿Their reckoning is only upon my Lord﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 113], ﴿and there is nothing of your reckoning upon them﴾. This is because they had criticised their religion and sincerity, so He said: their reckoning is necessarily upon them and does not pass over to you, just as your reckoning is upon you and does not pass over to them. ﴿So that you would drive them away﴾ is the answer to the negation, namely ﴿There is nothing of their reckoning upon you﴾. ﴿And you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ is the answer to the prohibition, namely ﴿And do not drive away﴾. It is also permissible that it be a conjunction with "so that you would drive them away" in the sense of causation, because his being a wrongdoer is caused by driving them away.

And thus We tested some of them through others. Likewise, We tested the rich through the poor with such a great trial. ﴿So that they would say﴾, that is, the rich: ﴿Is it these whom Allah has favoured from among us?﴾ That is, Allah has bestowed upon them the blessing of faith, while we are the foremost and the leaders, and they are the poor?! This is said in denial, meaning that people like them could not be upon the truth, and that they could not be the recipients of any favour from among their own kind. A similar verse is: ﴿Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 11]. ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who give thanks?﴾, that is, of those who are thankful for His blessing.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 54:

﴿And when those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: Peace be upon you.﴾ This may be a command to convey the peace of Allah to them, or a command to begin them with the greeting of peace, honouring them and comforting their hearts. Likewise His saying: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ is among what He tells them, to give them the good news of the breadth of Allah's mercy and His acceptance of their repentance. Its meaning: He has promised you mercy as a firm promise.

﴿Annahu﴾ (that He): the pronoun refers to the matter (shan, i.e. the pronoun of the case). ﴿whoever of you does evil﴾ — a sin — ﴿in ignorance﴾ is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: he commits it while ignorant of the harm attached to it; or he is made ignorant because he preferred disobedience over obedience. ﴿Then repents after it﴾ — after the evil, or the action.

﴿and makes amends﴾ — and makes his repentance sincere — ﴿then indeed He is Forgiving, Merciful.﴾ ﴿Annahu﴾ and ﴿fa-innahu﴾ are read by Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim (with the opening hamza of "annahu" as in the Shamī and ʿĀṣim reading). The first is a substitute (badal) for "mercy," and the second is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "so His matter is that He is Forgiving, Merciful." ﴿Annahu﴾ and ﴿fa-annahu﴾ are read by the Madanī reciters: the first is a substitute for "mercy," and the second is a subject (mubtada'). ﴿Innahu﴾ and ﴿fa-annahu﴾ are read by others, as a resumption (isti'nāf), as if mercy had been questioned, and it was said: "Whoever of you does evil..."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 55:

﴿Thus do We detail the signs, so that the way of the guilty may become clear﴾. And [the reading] with the yā' (ليستبين, "so that it may become clear") is that of Ḥamzah, ʿAlī and Abū Bakr. (سَبِيلُ المُجْرِمِينَ, "the way of the guilty") with the accusative (naṣb) is [the reading] of Madanī (Nāfiʿ of Madina); the rest read it in the nominative (rafʿ). Thus, when al-Sabīl (the way) is nominative, the verb is read with both tā' and yā', because it may be masculine or feminine (lit. "it is made masculine and it is made feminine"); and when al-Sabīl is accusative with the tā', it is addressed to the Messenger ﷺ. It is said: istabāna al-amr (the matter became clear) and tabayyana (became evident), and istabantuhu (I made it clear) and tabayyantuhu (I made it evident). The meaning: in like manner, with this clear detailing, We detail the signs of the Qur'an and set them out in describing the states of the guilty—those whose hearts are sealed and those whose acceptance of Islam is hoped for—and so that you might clarify their way, thereby treating each of them in the manner that he deserves to be treated, We have detailed that detailing.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 56:

﴿Say: Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides Allah.﴾ That is: I have been turned away and restrained, by the proofs of reason and revelation, from worshipping what you worship besides Allah. ﴿Say: I will not follow your whims.﴾ That is: I will not go along with your way which you have adopted in your religion, of following whims instead of following proof. This explains the cause which led them into misguidance. ﴿Then I would indeed have gone astray.﴾ That is: if I were to follow your whims, then I would be astray. ﴿And I am not of the guided ones﴾ in anything. He means: and you are likewise.

When he negated that desire should be followed, he pointed to what must be followed, saying: ﴿Say: Indeed I am upon clear evidence from my Lord.﴾ That is, I am upon clear evidence, from my knowledge of my Lord and that there is no deity besides Him.

﴿And you denied it﴾ in that you associated others with Him. It was also said: ﴿upon clear evidence from my Lord﴾ means upon proof from my Lord, which is the Qur'an.

﴿And you denied it﴾ refers to the clear evidence. The pronoun is masculine in accordance with interpreting it as the proof (al-burhan), or the clarification (al-bayan), or the Qur'an. He then followed this with what indicates that they deserve to be punished with the torment, so he said: ﴿What I have is not what you seek to hasten.﴾ He means the torment they sought in their saying: "Rain down on us stones from the sky" (Al-Anfal 8:32). ﴿The judgment belongs only to God﴾ regarding the delay of your punishment.

"Yaqussu al-haqq" (He relates the truth) is the reading of the Hijazi reader, and of ʿĀṣim (the Kufan reader). It means: He follows the truth and wisdom in what He decides and decrees, from qassa āthārahu (he traced his footsteps). The rest of the readers read "yaqḍi al-haqq" (He decides the truth), in all that He decides concerning delay and hastening. Thus "al-ḥaqq" means the judgment (al-qaḍāʾ). The word "al-ḥaqq" is an attribute of the verbal noun of "yaqḍi," and His saying ﴿and He is the best of deciders﴾ means: the best of those who judge with a true judgment, since al-faṣl (decision) is al-qaḍāʾ (judgment). The omission of the yāʾ from the written form follows the pronunciation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 58:

﴿Say: If what you are hastening for were within my power﴾, i.e., within my capacity and ability, ﴿the matter would have been decided between me and you﴾: I would have destroyed you immediately, out of anger for my Lord. ﴿And Allah knows best the wrongdoers﴾: so He sends down the punishment upon you at a time He knows to be more effective in deterring you.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 59:

﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He.﴾ "Al-mafatih" is the plural of "miftah" (key), and they are the treasuries of punishment and provision, or what is hidden from the servants of the reward, the punishment, the appointed terms, and the states (of things). The unseen is described as having keys by way of metaphor (isti'arah), because keys are the means by which one reaches what lies in treasuries that are secured with locks and bolts. Whoever knows its keys and how to open them can reach what is within. So the meaning is that He alone is the one who reaches the unseen things, and no one else can reach them, just as one who has the keys to the locks of the storehouses and knows how to open them is the one who reaches what is in the storehouses. It has been said: "With Him are the keys of the unseen," and "With you are the keys of the unseen"; whoever believes in His unseen, Allah will draw the veil over his faults. ﴿And He knows what is on the land﴾ of plants and animals.

﴿and the sea﴾ of living creatures, jewels, and other things.

﴿And not a leaf falls but He knows it﴾ "Ma" is for negation, and "min" is for totality (istighraq), meaning: He knows its number and its states before it falls and after it falls. ﴿Nor a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything moist or dry﴾ is coordinated with "leaf" and falls under its ruling.

﴿except that it is in a clear book﴾ is like a repetition of His saying "except that He knows it," because the meaning of "except that He knows it" and the meaning of "except that it is in a clear book" are one, namely the knowledge of Allah, or the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh).

Then He addressed the disbelievers with His words: ﴿And it is He who takes your souls by night﴾, that is, He seizes your selves from full activity during sleep. ﴿And He knows what you have committed (jaraḥtum) by day﴾, that is, what sins you have earned in it. ﴿Then He raises you up therein﴾, that is, then He wakes you up during the day. Or the sense is: then He raises you up during the day, and He knows what you have committed therein; so He put the earning first, because it is more important. It does not follow from this that He does not know what we commit by night, nor that He does not take our souls by day; thus the specification of one thing by mention does not indicate the negation of what is other than it. ﴿That a term appointed may be fulfilled﴾, that the appointed terms be completed in full. ﴿Then to Him is your return﴾, your return by resurrection after death. ﴿Then He will inform you of what you used to do﴾ in your nights and your days.

Some of the people of kalam (ahl al-kalam) said: each of these senses has a spirit (ruh) which is seized during sleep and then returned to it when sleep departs. As for the spirit by which the self (nafs) lives, it is not seized except at the end of the appointed term. By "spirits" are meant the meanings and powers that subsist in the senses, through which there is hearing, sight, grasping, walking and smelling. The meaning of ﴿then He raises you up therein﴾ is: He wakes you, and returns to you the spirits of the senses. Thus it is used as an argument against those who deny resurrection, for by sleep He removes the spirits of these senses, then returns them to them; so likewise He revives the souls after their death.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 61:

﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends over you guardians﴾ — angels who keep watch over your deeds; they are the noble recording ones (al-kiraman al-katibun), so that this would be more effective in deterring the servants from committing corruption (al-fasad), (p-511) when they reflect that their records are read out before the assembled witnesses. ﴿Until, when death comes to one of you﴾ — "until" (hatta) indicates the endpoint of the preservation of deeds; that is, this is the practice of the angels with the accountable person throughout the duration of life, until death comes to him. ﴿Our messengers take him in death﴾ — meaning they have fully taken his soul (istawfat ruhahu). They are the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt) and his assistants. (Tawaffihi and istawfihi) with imalah (vowel inclination) is recited by Hamzah. (Rusulana) is recited by Abu 'Amr. ﴿And they do not neglect﴾ — they do not delay, nor do they postpone.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 62:

﴿Then they are returned to Allah﴾, to His judgment and His recompense. That is, those who have died are returned by the return of the angels. ﴿Their true Master (mawla)﴾, their Owner, who manages their affairs. ﴿the Truth﴾, the Just, who never judges except with truth; these are two attributes of Allah. ﴿Surely judgment is His﴾ on that Day; there is no judgment in it for anyone other than Him.

﴿And He is the swiftest of those who reckon﴾, whom no reckoning distracts from another reckoning; He reckons all creation in the time it takes to milk a sheep. It has also been said: returning to the One who raised you is better than remaining with the one who harmed you.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 63:

﴿Say: "Who rescues you﴾ (yunjīkum) Ibn ʿAbbās (reads it as yunjīkum) ﴿from the darkness of land and sea?﴾ It is a metaphor for their dangers and terrors. Or, the darkness of the land: the thunderbolts; and the sea: the waves; and both occur in clouds and at night. ﴿You call upon Him﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to the object pronoun in "yunajjīkum." ﴿Humbly﴾ meaning openly displaying humility; it is a verbal noun (maṣdar) in the position of a circumstantial clause. Likewise ﴿and secretly﴾, meaning: keeping it hidden within yourselves. (khifyatan) wherever it occurs: Abū Bakr; and both are dialectal variants (lughatān). (la'in anjānā) ʿĀṣim. With imāla: Ḥamzah and ʿAlī. The rest read (anjaytanā). The meaning: they say, "If You deliver us..."

﴿From this﴾ darkness ﴿we will surely be among the thankful﴾ to God, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 64:

﴿Say, "It is Allah who delivers you from them and from every distress, yet you associate others with Him."﴾

٦٤ (Say: Allah delivers you) with the shaddah (intensive form, yunajjikum): this is the reading of Kufa (al-Kufi).

﴿from them﴾, that is, from the darknesses, ﴿and from every distress﴾ and grief, and sorrow.

﴿Yet you associate others with Him﴾, and do not give thanks.

﴿Say: "He is the Able"﴾, meaning He whom you know to be able, or He who has complete power. The lam [in al-qadir] may be the lam of al-'ahd (the lam of previous reference) or the lam of al-jins (the lam of genus).

﴿Over you to send a punishment from above you﴾, as He rained [stones] upon the people of Lut and upon the companions of the elephant.

﴿Or from beneath your feet﴾, as He drowned Pharaoh and caused Qarun to be swallowed up by the earth. Or [it means punishment] from the direction of your sultans and your rabble. Or it means the withholding of rain and of vegetation.

﴿Or to confuse you into sects﴾, or to mix you into factions divided over various desires, each faction among you following a leader (imam). The meaning of mixing them is that fighting breaks out among them, so they become entangled and intermingled in the thick of battle.

﴿And to make some of you taste the violence of others﴾, meaning that some of you kill others. Ba's means the sword. And from him (ﷺ): "I asked God, exalted is He, not to send a punishment upon my community from above them or from beneath their feet, and He granted me that. And I asked Him not to make their violence (ba's) among themselves, and He refused me. And Jibril informed me that the destruction of my community would be by the sword."

﴿See how We vary the signs﴾, through promise and warning, ﴿that they may understand﴾.

[Verse 6:66] "And your people denied it" — by the Qur'an, or by the punishment — "your people" meaning Quraysh, "while it is the truth" — i.e., the true reality, or that it must certainly befall them. "Say: I am not a guardian over you" — a keeper to whom your affair has been entrusted; I am only a warner.

﴿For every news⁠﴾ — for every matter that is announced, meaning: their being told that they will be punished, and their being warned of it. ﴿There is a fixed time⁠﴾ — a time of settling and occurrence that cannot be avoided. ﴿But you will come to know⁠﴾ — a threat.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 68:

﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our signs﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, meaning they engage in mockery of them and in disparaging them; and the Quraysh used to do this in their assemblies.

﴿Then turn away from them﴾, and do not sit with them, and rise up from them,

﴿until they engage in talk other than it﴾, other than the Qur'an, of what is permissible; then at that time it is permissible for you to sit with them. ﴿And if Satan causes you to forget﴾ what you were forbidden. (yunsiyannaka) is the reading of Ibn Amir (Shami). Nassa and Ansa are one and the same (in meaning).

﴿Then do not sit, after the remembrance﴾, after you have remembered, ﴿with the wrongdoing people﴾.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 69:

﴿And upon those who fear God there is nothing of their reckoning﴾ — of the reckoning of these people who plunge into the Qur'an with denial and mockery — ﴿of anything﴾, i.e., nothing falls upon the God-fearing who sit with them of what they are held accountable for of their sins.

﴿But﴾ it is incumbent upon them to remind them ﴿a reminder﴾ when they hear them plunging into it, by standing up away from them, showing their dislike of them, and admonishing them. The position of "dhikra" (a reminder) is in the accusative, i.e., "but they should remind them with a reminder," that is, a reminding; or it is in the nominative, the implied sense being "but upon them is a reminder," so "dhikra" is the subject (mubtada'), and the predicate (khabar) is omitted.

﴿So that they may fear God﴾ — so that they may avoid plunging into it out of shame, or out of dislike of its offensiveness to them.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on Surah 6, verse 70:**

﴿And leave those who have taken their religion﴾, the one they were charged with and called to, which is the religion of Islam.

﴿As amusement and diversion﴾: they mocked it and ridiculed it. The meaning of *dharhum* (leave them) is: turn away from them, and do not care about their denial and their mockery. *Al-lahw* (diversion) is that which occupies a person through desire or merriment.

﴿And the worldly life has deceived them. And remind with it﴾, i.e., admonish with the Qur'an, ﴿lest a soul be delivered to ruin for what it has earned﴾, out of fear that it will be handed over to destruction and punishment and held in pledge for the evil of what it has earned. The root of *al-ibsal* (being delivered to ruin) is prevention.

﴿It will have no protector besides Allah﴾, who would help it by force, ﴿nor any intercessor﴾, who would ward off [punishment] from it by request. In the sound view, there is no pause at *kasabat* (what it has earned), because His saying ﴿it will have no﴾ is a qualifier (*sifah*) of *nafs* (soul). The meaning is: remind with the Qur'an, lest a soul be delivered to ruin, lacking a protector and an intercessor for what it has earned.

﴿And if it offers every ransom﴾: *'adl* here is in the accusative as a verbal noun (*masdar*), meaning "and if it offers every ransom (*fida'*)". *Al-'adl* means the ransom, because the one who ransoms equalizes the one ransomed with its equivalent. The subject of ﴿it will not be taken﴾ is ﴿from it﴾, not the pronoun of *'adl*, because *'adl* here is a verbal noun, and taking cannot be attributed to it. As for His saying ﴿nor will any ransom be accepted from it﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 48], *'adl* there means the thing offered as ransom, so attributing the taking to it is valid.

﴿Those﴾ refers to those who took their religion as amusement and diversion. It is the subject (*mubtada'*), and the predicate (*khabar*) is: (p-514) ﴿those who have been delivered to ruin for what they have earned﴾. His saying ﴿for them is a drink of scalding water﴾, i.e., hot boiling water, is a second predicate (*khabar thani*) for *ula'ika*. The estimation is: "Those are the ones delivered to ruin; for them is a drink of scalding water." Or it may be a new (independent) sentence: ﴿and a painful punishment, because they used to disbelieve﴾, i.e., because of their disbelief.

**﴿Say﴾** to Abu Bakr, who says to his son ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who used to call his father to the worship of idols: "Shall we call upon" (أنَدْعُو), shall we worship, **﴿besides Allah﴾**, the one who harms and benefits, **﴿that which can neither benefit us﴾**, that which is not able to benefit us if we call upon it, **﴿nor harm us﴾** if we abandon it, **﴿and be turned back﴾** (وأنُرَدُّ), and be turned back, **﴿upon our heels﴾**, returning to polytheism, **﴿after Allah has guided us﴾** to Islam and rescued us from the worship of idols? **﴿Like one whom the devils have enticed﴾**, like one whom the ghūl (ghūlān) and the rebellious jinn have carried away.

The kāf (ك) is in the accusative position (فِي مَحَلِّ النَصْبِ), as a ḥāl (circumstantial clause, describing the state of the subject) referring to the pronoun in "نُرَدُّ عَلى أعْقابِنا". That is, the meaning is: "Shall we turn back, resembling the one whom the devils have enticed?" The verb is of the form istafʿala, from "hawā fī al-arḍ", meaning he went off into it. It is as if its meaning is: its desire was sought (طَلَبَتْ هُوِيَّهُ).

**﴿In the earth﴾**, in the desert wilderness (المَهْمَهِ), **﴿bewildered﴾**. This is a ḥāl (circumstantial clause) from the object of "istahwat-hu", meaning: lost and astray from the main road, not knowing how to act. **﴿He has companions﴾**, a group of companions, **﴿who call him to the guidance﴾**, to show him the way. The straight path was called guidance (الهُدى). They say to him: **﴿Come to us﴾**, while he has strayed into the wilderness following the jinn, and does not answer them or come to them.

This is based on what is said: that the jinn lead a person astray, and the ghūl overpower him. Thus the one who strays from the path of Islam, and follows the steps of Satan, is likened to that person, while the Muslims call him to it, but he does not turn to them.

**﴿Say: Indeed, the guidance of Allah﴾**, which is Islam, **﴿is the guidance﴾** alone, and whatever lies beyond it is misguidance. **﴿And we have been commanded﴾** (وَأُمِرْنا). Its position (مَحَلُّهُ) is in the accusative (النَصْبِ), by ʿaṭf (conjunction) upon the position of "إنَّ هُدى اللهِ هو الهُدى", since both are maqūl (things said), as if it were said: "Say this statement, and say: we have been commanded."

**﴿That we may submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾**

"And that establish prayer." The sense is: "We have been commanded to submit (aslama) to the Lord of the worlds, and [we have been commanded] that we establish prayer," i.e., for Islam and for the establishment of prayer (iqamat al-salat).

﴿And fear Him. And it is He to whom you will be gathered﴾ on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 73:

﴿And it is He who created the heavens and the earth with truth﴾: bi-l-hikmah (with wisdom), or muhiqqan (justly, rightfully).

﴿And the day He says, "Be," and it is,﴾ [this is] according to the reading of the predicate (khabar) rather than the answer. ﴿His word is the truth﴾ is a mubtada' (subject), and ﴿the day He says﴾ is its khabar (predicate), placed before it, as you say: "The day of Friday, your word is the truth," meaning: your word being the truth was on the day of Friday. Al-yawm (the day) here carries the meaning of al-hin (a time). The meaning is: He created the heavens and the earth with truth and wisdom, and at the time He says to any thing: "Be," and it is, that thing is His word, the truth and the wisdom; that is, nothing of the heavens and the earth or of the rest of the created beings comes into existence except out of wisdom and rightness.

﴿And His is the dominion﴾ is a mubtada' and khabar. ﴿The day the Trumpet is blown﴾ is a adverbial complement (zarf) for His saying ﴿And His is the dominion﴾. ﴿In the Trumpet﴾: it is al-qarn (the horn) in the dialect of Yemen, or the plural of surah (form/image).

﴿Knower of the unseen﴾: He is the Knower of the unseen ﴿and the visible﴾, that is, the hidden and the manifest. ﴿And He is the All-Wise﴾ in causing to perish and in giving life. ﴿the All-Aware﴾ of the reckoning and the recompense.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on Surah 6, verse 74:

﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar﴾. This is the name of his father, or his epithet (laqab), because the genealogists (*nassabin*) disagree that the name of his father was Tarikh. It is an explicative apposition (*'atf bayan*) to "his father". Its morphological pattern (*wazn*) is *fa'il*.

﴿Do you take idols as gods?﴾ This is an interrogation of rebuke (*istifham tawbikh*), meaning: "Do you take them as gods, when they do not deserve divinity?"

﴿Indeed, I see you and your people in manifest error.﴾

(p-516)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 75:

﴿And thus﴾ i.e., just as We showed him the ugliness of shirk, ﴿We showed Ibrahim the dominion (malakut) of the heavens and the earth﴾ i.e., We showed his insight (basirah) the subtle workings of the creation of the heavens and the earth. "Nuri" (We show) is the narration of a past state, and malakut is more emphatic than mulk (dominion), because the waw and the ta' are added for emphasis. Mujahid said: the seven heavens were opened up for him, so he looked at what is in them, until his gaze reached the Throne; and the seven earths were opened up for him, until he looked at what is in them. ﴿And that he might be among those who have certainty﴾ i.e., We did that, or so that he might draw inference (yastadall) ﴿and that he might be among those who have certainty﴾ by direct sight (ʿiyanan), just as he had certainty by demonstration (bayanan).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 76:

﴿When the night covered him over﴾, i.e., grew dark. This is a conjunction (ʿatf) upon ﴿Ibrahim said to his father﴾. His saying ﴿And thus did We show Ibrahim﴾ is a parenthetical clause (jumla iʿtiraḍiyya) placed between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined. ﴿He saw a star﴾, i.e., Venus, or Jupiter. His father and his people worshipped idols, the sun, the moon, and the stars, so he wished to alert them to the error in their religion, to guide them to the path of reflection and inference (al-nazar wa'l-istidlal), and to make them aware that correct reflection leads to the conclusion that none of these is a god, because of the evidence of contingency (dalil al-huduth) in them, and because they have a originator (muhdith) who originated them and a governor (mudabbir) who arranged their rising, their setting, their movement, their course, and all their other conditions. So when he saw the star which they used to worship, ﴿he said: This is my lord﴾, i.e., he said to them: ﴿This is my lord﴾ according to your claim, or the meaning is: "Is this my lord?", mocking them and denouncing them. The Arabs dispense with the interrogative particle by means of the intonation of the voice.
