The interjected phrase, which came between parts of the enumerated items, is an interjection not foreign to the enumeration, because God, exalted is He, bestowed favor upon His servants by creating the livestock for their benefit and by permitting it to them. Thus the interjection by way of argument against the one who prohibits them serves as an emphasis on the permissibility, and interjections in speech are only introduced for emphasis.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 6, verse 145:

﴿Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me﴾ i.e., at that time, or in the revelation of the Qur'an, because the revelation of the *sunnah* (the Prophet's teachings and practice) has forbidden other things. Or it means: among the livestock, because the verse concerns rejecting the *bahirah* (a she-camel whose ear was slit and released, in pre-Islamic custom) and its counterparts. As for the *mawquudhah* (an animal beaten or struck to death), the *mutaraddiyah* (an animal that falls from a height and dies), and the *nateehah* (an animal gored to death), they are of the carrion. In this there is a reminder that prohibition is established only by God's revelation and His law, not by the desires of the self.

﴿forbidden﴾: an animal whose eating is prohibited. ﴿to an eater who eats it﴾: to one who eats it. ﴿unless it be carrion﴾: unless the forbidden thing is carrion. The reading "an takuna" (that it be) is that of Makki (Ibn Kathir of Makkah), al-Shami (Ibn ʿAmir of Damascus), and Hamzah. The reading "maytatun" (carrion, in the nominative) is that of al-Shami.

﴿or blood poured forth﴾: flowing, liquid blood. Therefore the blood that remains in the meat, the liver, and the spleen is not forbidden. ﴿or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is impure﴾: it is *rijs* (impure, filthy). ﴿or an abomination﴾: this is coordinated with the accusative noun before it. The phrase ﴿for indeed it is impure﴾ is a parenthetical clause placed between the coordinated noun and the noun it is coordinated with. ﴿over which a name other than God's has been invoked﴾: this is in the accusative position as a qualifier of "abomination" (*fisqan*). That is, raising the voice over its slaughter in the name of other than God. It was called "abomination" (*fisq*) because of its deep immersion in the category of abomination. ﴿But whoever is compelled﴾: whoever is driven by necessity to eat something of these prohibited things. ﴿neither desiring nor transgressing﴾: not desiring to go against another person in the same necessity, leaving aside sharing with him. ﴿nor exceeding﴾: exceeding the measure of his need in consuming it. ﴿then indeed your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: He does not call him to account for it.

(p-٥٤٥)

﴿And to those who became Jews We forbade every animal with a hoof﴾, that is, every animal or bird that has a digit (*uṣbuʿ*). This includes camels and ostriches.

﴿And from the cattle and the sheep We forbade them their fats﴾. That is, We forbade them the flesh of every animal with a hoof and its fat, and every part of it. From cattle and sheep, He forbade only the fats, which are the *thurub* (the fat covering the intestines) and the fat of the kidneys.

﴿Except what their backs carry﴾, meaning except what is attached to the backs and sides of the *sahfah* (the fat spread over the back). ﴿Or the entrails﴾, or what is attached to the intestines. Its singular is *ḥāwiyāʾ* or *ḥawiyyah*.

﴿Or what is mixed with bone﴾, which is the fat of the tail, or the marrow.

﴿That﴾ is the second object of His saying ﴿We requited them﴾, and the sense is: We requited them with that ﴿for their transgression﴾, because of their wrongdoing. ﴿And indeed We are truthful﴾ in what We have informed of. And how can we give thanks to One who caused their disobedience by forbidding the lawful, and our predecessors' disobedience by permitting the unlawful? As He said: ﴿And He has pardoned you. So now, lie with them﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 187].

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 147:

﴿Then if they deny you﴾ concerning what I have revealed to you of this, ﴿then say: Your Lord is of boundless mercy﴾ by which He gives the deniers respite and does not hasten to punish them,

﴿and His punishment is not averted from the guilty people﴾ — His punishment, despite the vastness of His mercy, when it comes. So do not be deceived by the vastness of His mercy into neglecting fear of His vengeance.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 148:

﴿Those who associated partners [with Allah] will say﴾: a report of what they will say in the future. ﴿"Had Allah willed, we would not have associated [anything with Him], nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything."﴾ But He willed [it], so this is our excuse. They mean: their associating partners, the associating of their fathers, and their forbidding what Allah has made lawful for them, occurred by His will, and had it not been for His will, none of that would have happened. ﴿Likewise did those before them deny﴾: meaning, just as you were denied, those who came before them denied, and they clung to the like of this. It did not benefit them, since they did not say it out of conviction; rather they said it mockingly, and because they made His will a proof for themselves that they were excused by it. This is rejected, not the affirmation of the will. Or the meaning of "will" here is "approval," as al-Hasan said, i.e.: Allah approved of our associating and that of our fathers; the association is willed but is not approved. Do you not see that He said: ﴿Then had He willed, He would have guided you all﴾? He informed that had He willed guidance for them, all of them would have believed, but He did not will belief for all of them; rather He willed belief for some and disbelief for others. So the will must be interpreted here as we have mentioned, to avoid contradiction. ﴿Until they tasted Our punishment﴾: until We sent down the punishment upon them. ﴿Say: Do you have any knowledge﴾: any matter known which may validly be used as evidence for what you claim, ﴿so that you bring it out for us﴾: so that you display it. ﴿You only follow conjecture, and you only guess﴾: you are lying.

Say: "To God belongs the conclusive proof." Against you, by His commands and prohibitions. You have no proof against God by His will. ﴿Then had He willed, He would have guided you all.﴾ That is, had He willed your guidance. By this, the assault of the Mu'tazila (the rationalist school that holds that human beings create their own actions) is nullified.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 150:

﴿Say: Bring forth your witnesses﴾ (hallumma shuhadaakum): Bring your witnesses and bring them near. In this expression (kalima), the singular and the plural, and the masculine and the feminine, are equal according to the people of the Hijaz (al-Hijaziyyun). The Banu Tamim (Banu Tamim) make it feminine and plural (tu'annithu wa-tajma'u) ﴿those who testify that God has forbidden this﴾, that is, they claim it to be forbidden. ﴿If they testify, do not testify along with them﴾, meaning, do not accept for them what they testify to, and do not confirm them; for if you accept it for them, it is as though you had testified with them the same testimony as theirs, and so you would be one of them. ﴿And do not follow the desires of those who deny Our signs﴾. The use of the apparent noun in place of the pronoun (min wad' al-zahir mawdi' al-mudmar) serves to indicate that whoever denies the signs of God is a follower of his desire, since if he had followed the proof he would not be anything but one who confirms the signs and affirms the oneness of God. ﴿And those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾ are the polytheists, ﴿and they ascribe equals to their Lord﴾, that is, they make the idols equal (yusawwuna al-asnam) to Him.

﴿Say﴾ to those who forbade the tilth and the cattle, ﴿come﴾. This is from the specific term (*khass*) that came to be used generally. Its origin is that one who is in a high place says it to one who is below him. Then it became common until it was used generally. ﴿I will recite what your Lord has forbidden﴾, which your Lord forbade, ﴿to you﴾, from the relative clause (*silah*) of "forbade." ﴿That you associate nothing with Him﴾: *an* is an explanatory particle (*mufassirah*) for the act of reciting, and *la* is for prohibition (*nahy*).

﴿And good treatment of parents﴾, meaning: and be good to your parents. Since the obligation of goodness is a prohibition of neglecting goodness, it is mentioned among the forbidden things. The same ruling applies to what follows it of commands.

﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty﴾, meaning: because of poverty, and out of fear of it, like His saying: ﴿for fear of poverty﴾ [al-Isra: 31]. ﴿We provide for you and for them﴾, because the provision of servants is upon their master. ﴿And do not approach the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden﴾: what is apparent is what is between you and the creation, and what is hidden is what is between you and God. ﴿What is apparent﴾ is a substitute (*badal*) for ﴿the indecencies﴾.

﴿And do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right﴾, such as retaliation (*qisas*), killing for apostasy (*ridda*), and stoning (*rajm*). ﴿That He has enjoined upon you﴾, i.e., what has been mentioned in detail, your Lord has commanded you to preserve. ﴿That you may understand﴾, so that you may understand its greatness before God.

(p-548)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 152:

﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the way that is best﴾ — except with the manner that is best, namely safeguarding it and making it grow, ﴿until he reaches his maturity (ashuddahu)﴾. Ashuddah: the age of his reaching puberty (hulm). Then hand it over to him. Its singular is shadd, like fals and aflus (the plural forms of fals, a coin).

﴿And give full measure and weight with justice﴾ — with equity and fairness.

﴿We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾ — except what it can bear, and which it is not unable to do. The command to give full measure and weight was followed by this because observing the limit of justice, in which there is neither excess nor deficiency, may involve hardship; so He commanded that one reach the capacity, and that what lies beyond it is pardoned.

﴿And when you speak, be just﴾ — be truthful, ﴿even if it concerns a near relative﴾ — even if the one being addressed, or the one against whom one testifies in a testimony or in something else, is a relative of the speaker, as in His saying: ﴿even if it be against yourselves, or your parents and close relatives﴾ [al-Nisa: 135].

﴿And fulfil the covenant of God﴾ — the covenant of the Day of the Covenant (mithaq), or in commands and prohibitions, [promises and threats], vows and oaths. ﴿That is what He has enjoined upon you﴾, i.e., what has passed. ﴿That you may remember (la'allakum tadhakkarun)﴾ — with the lightened form wherever it occurs for Hamzah, Ali and Hafs, by omitting one of the two tas; others read it with the doubled form, the original being tatadhakkarun, in which the second ta is assimilated into the dhal, i.e., He commanded you so that you may take heed.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 153:

﴿And that this is My path﴾ And because this is My path, it is the cause (ʿillah) for following it, with an implied lām (li-anna). "Wa-anna" with the light (takhfif) pronunciation is read by Ibn ʿĀmir (Shāmī), and its original form is "wa-annahu," with the hāʾ being the pronoun of the matter and the subject (ḍamīr al-shaʾn wa-l-ḥadīth). "Wa-inna" with a fresh start (ʿalā al-ibtidāʾ) is read by Ḥamzah and ʿAlī.

﴿straight﴾ is a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl). ﴿So follow it, and do not follow the [other] ways﴾ the paths that differ in religion, from Judaism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, and all the innovations and misguidances.

﴿so that they will separate you from His way﴾ that they will scatter you, like the Sabaʾ, away from the straight path of God, which is the religion of Islam. It has been narrated that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) drew a straight line, then said: "This is the path of guidance and the path of God, so follow it." Then he drew on each side six lines, slanting, and said: "These are ways; on each way there is a devil calling to it, so avoid them." Then he recited this verse. "Then each one of the twelve [paths] becomes six paths, so there are seventy-two."

From Ibn ʿAbbas, may God be pleased with him and his father: these verses are muhkamat; no part of them has been abrogated by anything from all the books.

From Kaʿb: indeed these verses are the first thing in the Torah.

﴿That is what He has enjoined upon you, so that you may be God-fearing﴾ so that you may be on the hope of attaining taqwa. He mentioned first "you may understand" (taʿqilūn), then "you may remember" (tadhakkarūn), then "you may be God-fearing" (tattaqūn), because when they understand they reflect, then they remember, that is, they take heed and so they guard against the prohibited things.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 154:

﴿Then We gave Moses the Book, complete﴾. That is: then I inform you that We gave it; or it is a conjunction with "Say" (qul), meaning: then say, "We gave it." Or "thumma" here comes with the meaning of "wa" (and) in joining sentences, as in His saying: ﴿Then God is Witness﴾ [Yunus: 46].

﴿Upon the one who did good﴾: upon the one who was a doer of good and righteous, meaning the class of those who do good. The evidence for this is the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud (ʿAbd Allah): "upon those who did good." Or it means Moses, peace be upon him, that is: as a completion of the honour bestowed upon the servant who perfected obedience in conveying everything he was commanded.

﴿And a detailed explanation of all things﴾: and a clear, detailed exposition of everything they need in their religion.

﴿And guidance and mercy, that perhaps they﴾: that is, the Children of Israel, ﴿in the meeting with their Lord would believe﴾: would affirm.

This and the Qur'an (هَذا): that is, the Qur'an,

﴿a Book We have sent down, blessed﴾, abundant in good, ﴿so follow it and be mindful of God﴾ by not opposing it, ﴿that you may be shown mercy﴾, so that you may receive mercy.

﴿Lest you should say﴾ (meaning: out of aversion to your saying, or lest you say).

﴿The Book was sent down only upon two groups before us﴾, that is, the People of the Torah (Tawrat) and the People of the Gospel (Injil). This is evidence that the Magians (al-Majus) are not People of a Book. ﴿And we were indeed unaware of their study﴾, that is, of their recitation of their books, ﴿having no knowledge of any of that.﴾ "In" (inna) here is the light (mukhaffafa) form of the heavy (thaqila) one, and the lam is the distinguishing particle that separates it from the negating "in." The original is: "Indeed, we were unaware of their study," with the hā' being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-sha'n), and the address is to the people of Makkah. The purpose is to establish the proof against them by the sending down of the Qur'an upon Muhammad (ﷺ), so that they would not say on the Day of Resurrection: "The Torah and the Gospel were sent down upon two groups before us, and we were unaware of what was in them."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 157:

﴿Or you should say﴾ lest you say ﴿If the Book had been sent down to us, we would surely have been better guided than they﴾ owing to the keenness of our minds, the acuteness of our understanding, and the abundance of our memorization of the Days of the Arabs (ayyam al-Arab, the famous battles and events of pre-Islamic Arabia). ﴿Now there has come to you a clear proof from your Lord﴾ meaning: if you are truthful in what you used to claim about yourselves, then there has come to you that which contains the radiant clarification and the decisive argument. Thus the condition is omitted, and this is among the most excellent of ellipses. ﴿And a guidance and a mercy.﴾ ﴿So who is more unjust than one who denies the signs of Allah﴾ after he has come to know their soundness and truthfulness, ﴿and turns away from them﴾ meaning: turns aside. ﴿We shall repay those who turn away from Our signs with a terrible punishment﴾ and it is: the utmost in severity ﴿for what they used to turn away from﴾ by their aversion.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 158:

﴿Are they waiting?﴾ That is: We have established the proofs of Divine Oneness and the confirmation of the Prophethood, and We have nullified the error they hold to. So what are they waiting for, in abandoning error after these [proofs]? ﴿Except that the angels come to them﴾, that is, the angels of death, to seize their souls. (﴿yaʼtiyahum﴾) is read by Hamzah and ʻAli (as yaʼtiyahum, with the verb in the masculine form).

﴿Or that your Lord comes﴾, that is, the command of your Lord, which is the punishment, or the Resurrection. This is because the "coming" (ityan) is ambiguous (mutashabih), whereas the coming of His command is explicitly stated (mansus ʻalayhi) and clear (muhkam), so the ambiguous is referred back to it. ﴿Or that some of the signs of your Lord come﴾, that is, the portents of the Hour, such as the rising of the sun from its west, and other things. ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, a soul will not benefit from its faith﴾ because it is not a faith of free choice; rather it is the faith of repelling punishment and calamity from themselves. ﴿Which it had not believed before﴾ is a description of "soul" (nafsan).

﴿Or it had not earned good through its faith﴾, that is, sincerity. Just as the faith of the disbeliever is not accepted after the rising of the sun from its west, the sincerity of the hypocrite is also not accepted, nor is his repentance. Its implied sense is: the faith of one who did not believe does not benefit, nor does the repentance of one who did not repent beforehand. ﴿Say: Wait﴾ for one of the three signs, ﴿indeed we are waiting﴾ for you, for one of them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 159:

﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion﴾ — they differed concerning it and became sects, just as the Jews and the Christians differed. And in the hadith: "The Jews split into seventy-one sects, all of them in the Abyss (al-Hawiyah) except one, which is the saved one (al-Najiyah), and the Christians split into seventy-two sects, all of them in the Abyss except one, and my community will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Abyss except one, and it is al-Sawad al-A'zam (the great majority)." And in another narration: "And it is what I am upon and my Companions." It has been said: "They divided their religion (dinahum)," so they believed in some of it and disbelieved in some of it. (Faraqu dinahum) is the reading of Hamzah and Ali, meaning: they abandoned it. ﴿And they became sects (shiya')﴾, groups, each faction following a leader of its own. ﴿You have no part in them in anything﴾, meaning: no part in being asked about them and their division, or in their punishment. ﴿Their affair is only with Allah; then He will inform them of what they used to do﴾, and so He will recompense them for that.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 160:

﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like of it.﴾ Its implied sense is: ten good deeds like it; except that the distinguishing attribute of the category (ṣifat al-jins) has been placed in the position of the thing it qualifies (al-mawṣūf). ﴿And whoever brings an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its like, and they will not be wronged.﴾ [That is:] by a reduction in reward or an increase in punishment.

﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me﴾ (*rabbiya*): Abu ʿAmr and the Madinan reader read it as *rabbiya* (with a fatḥa on the final yāʾ).

﴿to a straight path, a correct religion﴾ is in the accusative as a *badal* (substitution, i.e., a replacement apposition) for the place of ﴿to a straight path﴾, because its meaning is: "He has guided me to a path," as is evidenced by His saying: ﴿and guide you to a straight path﴾ [al-Fath: 20]. *Qiyaman* (قِيَمًا) and *qayyiman* (قَيِّمًا): the form is *fayyal* from *qāma*, like *sayyid* from *sāda*, and it is more intensive than *qā'im*. (*Qayyiman*) is read by the Kufan and Syrian readers. It is a verbal noun (*maṣdar*) in the sense of *qiyām*, and it is described by it.

﴿the religion of Abraham﴾ is an *ʿatf bayān* (explicative apposition, i.e., an apposition that clarifies the preceding term). ﴿a ḥanīf﴾ is a *ḥāl* (circumstantial accusative) from "Abraham." ﴿And he was not among the polytheists﴾ who associate partners with Allah, O assembly of Quraysh.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 162:

﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer (ṣalāt) and my sacrifice (nusuk)﴾ meaning: my worship (ʿibādatī). The nāsik is the ʿābid (one who worships). Or: my slaughter (dhabḥī), or my pilgrimage (ḥajjī).

﴿and my living and my dying﴾ and what I do in my life, and what I die upon of faith and righteous deeds.

﴿are for God, Lord of the worlds﴾, sincerely for His Face. (Maḥyāya wa-mamātī) with the first yāʾ sukūn and the second yāʾ fatḥah: Madanī (the reading of the people of Madinah); and the reverse of it for others.

ﷺ-free passage; translate faithfully.

"﴿There is no partner to Him﴾ in any of that. ﴿And with that﴾ sincerity ﴿I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims﴾, because the submission (islam) of every prophet precedes the submission of his community."

"Say, "Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, while He is the Lord of all things?"" This is a reply to their urging him to worship their gods. The interrogative particle (al-hamzah) is for denial, meaning: I deny that I would seek a lord other than Him. The fronting of the object (taqdim al-maf'ul) indicates that it is more important.

"And He is the Lord of all things." Everything other than Him is one who is lordship-owned (marbub), and there is no one in existence who possesses lordship (al-ruburiyyah) except Him.

"And no soul earns [sin] except against itself." This is a reply to their saying: "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins" (al-'Ankabut: 12), and "No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another" (ﷺ-less). That is: no sinful soul shall be seized (p-553) for the sin of another soul. "Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about what you used to dispute" concerning the religions that you divided into sects.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 165:

﴿And it is He who has made you successors (khalā'if) upon the earth﴾ Because Muhammad ﷺ is the seal of the prophets (khatam al-nabiyyin), his community has succeeded all other nations. Or, because some of them succeed others. Or, they are the vicegerents (khulafa') of God on His earth, possessing it and exercising authority over it. ﴿And He has raised some of you above others in degrees﴾ in nobility, in provision, and other things. ﴿Degrees (darajat)﴾ is a second object. Or the implied sense is "to degrees." Or it stands in the position of a verbal noun (masdar), as if it were said: "an elevation after an elevation."

﴿That He may test you in what He has given you﴾ in what He has bestowed upon you of the blessing of rank and wealth, how you will give thanks for that blessing, and how the noble will deal with the lowly, the rich with the poor, and the owner with the owned. ﴿Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment﴾ for those who disbelieve. ﴿And indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ for those who give thanks for them. He described the punishment as swift because what is coming is near. ﴿And the matter of the Hour is but as a glance of the eye or even nearer﴾ [al-Nahl: 77]. From the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever recites the first three verses of al-An'am in the morning, God the Exalted will appoint seventy thousand angels to guard him, and will write for him the like of their deeds until the Day of Resurrection."
